features.description: Plan for memory (spec §4.6, D3, D6): the three JSONL schemas, the pure rules as named functions, how n8n reads/writes the files, the code-node sync mechanism, and docs/memory.md for Michael.
steps: docs/plans/2026-10-22-B3-memory.md exists with: the schema of concepts.jsonl (id, term, explanation, first_report, times_referenced, understanding unknown|shaky|understood, last_checked, updated_at), questions.jsonl (id, run, feature, question, options, recommendation, status open|answered|withdrawn, answer, answered_at, via, first_asked_report, first_asked_at, event, updated_at) and reports.jsonl (id, date, event, runs, concepts_explained, questions_asked, usage, cost_usd, path); one row per entity, newest row wins on reread.

The plan names the pure functions in lib/memory.js with signatures and the rules each enforces: selectConcepts(glossary, concepts) -> {full, brief, again} (unknown -> full; understood or unknown-but-explained -> brief with first_report; shaky -> again); matchQuestions(parked, questions) -> {new, followUp, answered}; applyReport(memory, reportMeta, introduced, asked) -> new rows; gradeAnswers(grades, concepts) -> updated rows; parseJsonl(text) -> {rows, skipped}.

The plan describes the n8n side: workflows/30-memory.json as a sub-workflow (Execute Workflow Trigger, `op: load|save`), Read/Write Files nodes on `{{ $env.REPORTER_FILES_DIR }}/memory/*.jsonl`, rewrite-whole-file semantics (no append mode in the node), the rig's tests/workflows/rig-memory.json driver webhook, and the D6 sync (`scripts/sync-code-nodes.mjs` map of node name -> lib file, `--check` mode, tests/checks/code-sync.sh).

The plan outlines docs/memory.md (what each file is, how Michael corrects a row by editing the file, that restic backs it up via /srv/n8n) and lists the unit tests B3-02 will write and the E2E checks B3-03 will add, by name.

features.description: lib/memory.js pure rules with node --test unit tests, plus the Code-node sync script and drift check (D6), wired into the suite before the container starts.

lib/memory.js has no `require`/`import` and no top-level `return`; the tests load it with `vm.runInNewContext(src + '\n({selectConcepts, matchQuestions, applyReport, gradeAnswers, parseJsonl})')`.

scripts/sync-code-nodes.mjs reads a map in scripts/code-nodes.json (`workflow file -> {node name -> lib file}`), writes `<lib source>\n// --- glue (generated)\nreturn main($input.all().map(i => i.json));` into each node's jsCode, and `--check` exits 1 with the node name when the JSON differs; tests/checks/code-sync.sh wraps it and runs in the suite before the container starts, alongside `node --test tests/unit/` as `PASS unit tests`.

Deliberately editing a synced node's jsCode in a scratch copy makes `node scripts/sync-code-nodes.mjs --check` fail (shown in the progress entry), and `bash -n`/`node --check` pass on every file touched.
